articles.title: ‘It’s problematic’: Concern as ‘skinny jabs’ maker sponsors Vogue World event
articles.summary: Partnership between Mounjaro maker Eli Lilly and fashion giant, suggests thinness is an aspiration, say critics. The fifth iteration of Vogue World, overseen by Anna Wintour, took place in Milan on Tuesday night.
body: Eli Lilly, an American pharmaceutical company that manufactures a wide range of medicines, including weight-loss jabs Mounjaro and the Foundayo pill, was listed in the event credits as one of its “fashion adjacent” sponsors.

The pharmaceutical company also sponsored the 2025 Vogue World in Hollywood, as well as the Met Gala livestream earlier this year, which included a promotional video starring the actor Patrick Schwarzenegger and the fashion brand Public School.

While the ongoing partnership did not explicitly link Mounjaro or Foundayo with Vogue, the marriage of high-profile fashion events and a weight-loss drug manufacturer has attracted fierce criticism from eating disorder charities and academics.

These groups have long believed that the fashion industry promotes thinness by habitually casting very thin models in catwalk shows, editorials and advertising, and warned of the negative impact this could have.

articles.title: Camo’s back: noughties pop’s military style is on the march again
articles.summary: A look evoking memories of All Saints and Destiny’s Child has fashion editors, Brad Pitt and the high street all blending in. Discussing their style while in All Saints, Nicole and Natalie Appleton said earlier this year that some things don’t change: “Army trousers and combat trousers will always…
body: If, for a long time after All Saints’ noughties heyday, the sisters would have known this look was not the height of fashion, things have changed in 2026. Judging by those attending shows at London fashion week this month, camo is very much back.

Worn with heels, beaded flats, camisoles and shirting, camo trousers became a standout front-row trend, one that had first been spotted at Copenhagen fashion week in August. Vogue described it as “a clear winner among the trends we spotted outside the shows”. Fashion editors aren’t alone either: celebrities including Alexa Chung and Iris Law have worn camo recently. And Brad Pitt, promoting his new survival movie Heart of the Beast, looked the part wearing camo trousers and matching jacket this month.

Hetty Mahlich, a brand editor at Burberry, was photographed wearing her army surplus camo pants at fashion week. She likes the way they can give a sense of contrast to an outfit: “They go with a vintage nightdress or a white baby tee, but they’re also great with a heel as I never like feeling too dressed up.”

articles.title: ‘I’d like to explain why I was such a monster back then’: six writers on the apologies they wish they’d made
articles.summary: From making life hell for a young teacher to doubting the motives of a caring foster mother, Olivia Petter, Derek Owusu, Annie Lord and other writers repent for past bad behaviour. At school, I was not a good girl.
body: At school, I was not a good girl. Actually, that’s putting it mildly: I was an emotional terrorist hellbent on inflicting torture and humiliation on my year 6 teacher, Ms Hill, one whoopee cushion at a time. That’s how it began, anyway, but like all crimes, mine followed a strategic pattern of escalation, carefully executed alongside my best friend and accomplice.

We started small: bringing spiders into Ms Hill’s classroom; writing silly notes on the whiteboard; replacing her precious chocolate digestives with stale biscuits from the dining hall. Then we took things further, hiding in cupboards behind her desk and jumping out to frighten her halfway through lessons, and, on one occasion, exploiting the bathroom’s faulty taps to flood the entire thing over lunchtime.

None of this was OK. In fact, it was downright awful, a symptom of reckless malevolence fuelled by boredom and entitlement. We were just unhappy kids who wanted to watch the world burn – an operation that poor Ms Hill bore almost all of the brunt of. To be clear, we never did anything that would constitute harassment, but our pranks were consistent and cruel.
points: From making life hell for a young teacher to doubting the motives of a caring foster mother, Olivia Petter, Derek Owusu, Annie Lord and other writers repent for past bad behaviour.

articles.title: ‘I turbocharged my career then pressed eject’: why couples are getting divorced later
articles.summary: Financial pressures, legal changes and shifting attitudes may help explain why couples are staying married for longer. “We don’t know anyone whose marriage hit the skids after just a few years,” Celia said, reflecting on her divorce.
body: It took Celia two years to initiate divorce after realising her 12-year marriage wasn’t going anywhere – and the latest figures show this experience is increasingly common, with marriages that end in divorce now lasting longer than at any point since records began.

“I approached it very methodically,” the AI analyst said. “I knew that women almost always end up financially worse off after divorce, especially where there are children concerned, so I took the time I needed to turbocharge my career before pressing ‘eject’.”
It helped, Celia said, that she and Martyn, her former husband, had been in their 40s when they got married.

“Because we were older and wiser, we took the time to try to mend our relationship instead of rushing off to start a new life,” she said. “When that didn’t work, Martyn was mature enough to know it was best for the children, me and us that he subtly left me alone to get to where I needed to be before we formally called time on the relationship.”

articles.title: Where to Get Pizza in Naples, Italy, Home of the Original Margherita Pie
articles.summary: The best pizza in the city, according to a longtime visitor.
body: Ask 10 Neapolitans about where to find the best pizza in Naples, and you will probably get ten different answers. Nipping down to the pizzeria ‘sotto casa’ (on the doorstep) is a bit like popping into your local pub for a pint, a cheap and cheerful night out with friends and neighbours and a chance to catch up on the local gossip.

Many of these places remain way beyond the tourist radar, but central Naples is stuffed with pizzerias and standards are generally high, so you can’t go far wrong; a mediocre pizza just doesn’t cut the mustard in this food-obsessed city. One rule of thumb is to always choose somewhere displaying the VPN sign outside—this stands for Verace Pizza Napoletana, and guarantees that the pizza will be made according to an exacting set of criteria.

The first pizza margherita was created in Naples in 1889 by Raffaele Esposito at Pizzeria Brandi (still in business) for the visit of King Umberto I of Savoy and Queen Margherita. Topped with red tomatoes, white mozzarella and green basil, it recalled the Italian flag and today, it is the touchstone by which any pizzaiolo worth his dough should be judged; there is nowhere to hide with a margherita.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Melting Dress Revives One of Fashion’s Great Runway Experiments
articles.summary: For the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, Rodrigo enlisted the iconic and innovative designer Hussein Chalayan to make a dress that dissolves under water.
body: Olivia Rodrigo has always understood the art of a good fashion reference and a costume change. On the GUTs tour, she had a rotation of slogan tees for the encore that changed from city to city. Her “ drop dead ” music video was jam-packed with sartorial tributes to Sofia Coppola and Jane Birkin. Styled by Chloe and Chenelle Delgadillo, she’s established an on-stage wardrobe rooted in riot grrrl-esque aesthetics and romantic shapes.

On the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, though, Rodrigo swerved the backstage quick-change, wearing a dress that transformed while she was still wearing it. Performing “The Cure” at Hartford’s PeoplesBank Arena on September 25, she appeared in a pristine white collared mini dress with a sweet pleated skirt. Then, as the song reached its climax and Rodrigo repeated, “ I’m unraveled, I’m unraveled...,” artificial rain began to pour from above. The white outer layer started to disintegrate before the audience’s eyes, eventually washing away to reveal a fire-red corseted bodysuit and miniskirt underneath—a pleasingly literal interpretation of the tour’s title.
points: For the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, Rodrigo enlisted the iconic and innovative designer Hussein Chalayan to make a dress that dissolves under water.

articles.title: Beauty Marks: The Best Beauty Looks of the Week
articles.summary: Fashion month is in full swing, and the best beauty looks of the week nodded to what’s in store: expect 3D nails, skin-forward glam, and blush, blush, blush!
body: Welcome back to Beauty Marks: Vogue ’s weekly edition of the best moments in celebrity beauty, from Vogue editors’ IG feeds, and all the glam of the fashion and pop culture landscapes. Each week, we curate the nail art to pin for your next nail appointment, new recruits to ‘Team Bob’, and major red carpet moments from the week’s most glamorous affairs. As always, it’s as much about celebrity beauty as it is about the makeup artists, hairstylists, and nail artists, as well as the creators crafting the trends you’re about to see everywhere.

This week, the best beauty looks played with shimmer and metallics: golden eyeshadow that pops, honey-blonde waves, nails glossy and chrome. Take Simone Ashley, for one, whose warm pink blush and glowing contour amped up her already sculptural features. Then there was Florence Pugh, who continues to embrace soft romance with delicate, sumptuously blonde waves tied up with a sweet black ribbon. Fashion Month is in full swing, too, and the beauty details hint at the biggest trends for the season ahead: expect skin-forward complexions, 3D nails, innovative eyeliner, and ’60s vibes.

articles.title: Inside Dove Cameron’s Final Fitting for Her “Celestial” Valentino Wedding Dress in Rome
articles.summary: See a first look at Dove Cameron’s custom Valentino wedding dress here, shared exclusively with Vogue. The musician and actor tied the knot with former Måneskin frontman Damiano David in a ceremony in Tuscany this weekend.
body: Dove Cameron and Damiano David are officially married! As shared exclusively with Vogue, the couple tied the knot this weekend at a private ceremony in Tuscany—and just four days before the wedding weekend celebrations, we joined Dove in Rome to pay a visit to the Valentino ateliers in Rome and try on her wedding dress for the very last time.

“Ciao, Vogue!” the musician and actor says before the final fitting, sitting at an outdoor café and reflecting on the experience of planning the wedding. “I never really dreamed about what my wedding would look like when I was a little girl—I think I wanted to rent out Carnegie Hall and enter in a big, black dress made out of feathers and have a 32-piece orchestra playing,” she says. And while she jokingly describes herself as “wildly unprepared” for the wedding ahead, she also notes: “It feels right. It feels natural. It feels easy. It feels like a natural, beautiful next step. I don't know how else to describe it. I'm in love, [and] we're throwing a big party.”

articles.title: Comedian Edy Modica Is Just Like You (But Funnier)
articles.summary: It’s been a busy few years for Modica, who just released her first stand-up special, “I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks).”
body: When comedian Edy Modica arrives at the Condé Nast offices in downtown Manhattan, she looks as if she’s just wrapped filming on a Bravo show—her hoop earrings are sparkly and huge, her heeled denim boots coordinate perfectly with her long denim shorts, and a nameplate necklace spells out EDY. As I soon learn, that is, in fact, exactly the case; Modica is coming straight from guest-bartending on an episode of Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen.

Modica is promoting I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks), her chatty, confrontational, and sometimes crude debut special. (One of its best parts revolves around a young Modica browsing sites with names like “boobs.com” and “sex.com.”) But her strong and singular comedic voice has remained largely unchanged since I saw her perform a fully nude show at Williamsburg’s now-shuttered Annoyance Theatre a decade ago. I struggle with how to bring it up without sounding like a pervert, but Modica excitedly tells me that she remembers the set well; in fact, both of her parents were in attendance.
points: It’s been a busy few years for Modica, who just released her first stand-up special, “I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks).”
